issue.title: renderComponentToString does not reflect `<select>` value

repository.name: react
repository.description: The library for web and native user interfaces.

issue.body:
`React.renderComponentToString` does not appear to render selection state for `select` elements. Given [this example](http://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1408993/react-html-render-issue.html): ``` html
``` The HTML is rendered like this: ![screen shot 2014-06-11 at 7 58 55 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/4433/3252601/5f07db2c-f1c4-11e3-8a34-9af2ae003d0b.png) Which means that selection state is only applied once the markup hits the client. The only way to preserve selection state through `React.renderComponentToString` is to set the `selected` property on each `option`, which results in these warnings on both the client and server: ![screen shot 2014-06-11 at 8 01 38 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/4433/3252621/c33d1936-f1c4-11e3-925a-8ee3cc7edaa9.png) In my opinion, the server and client experience should be identical, and selection state should not depend on whether the client JavaScript has loaded.

body:
Googling this bug turned up nothing given the recent API change from `React.renderComponentToString` to `React.renderToString`.

In the interests of helping others to avoid an hour or so of inexplicable behaviour, note that Select elements that are rendered to a string will not provide checked attributes to their child options as of React 0.12.1.

http://jsfiddle.net/t9wee5tr/3/
+1 for putting this back to the agenda.
